title: Modularize fallback transitions and reduce contention in regional mapping
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
We have observed increased CPU and mutex contention originating from the smart routing regional mappers and the monolithic fallback state machine during high-concurrency workloads. This ticket refactors the fallback transition path into a modular, pluggable transition engine and reduces global lock contention in regional mapping logic. Goals are to lower 95th/99th tail latency for routing decision path, reduce CPU utilization under heavy traffic, and make fallback behavior testable and replaceable without touching hot-path routing code.

Problem details:
- Regional mapper performs a sequence of synchronous lookups and atomic updates under a single global lock when evaluating region affinity. Under bursty loads this causes stall behavior and increased scheduling latency.
- Fallback transitions are implemented as a monolithic state machine embedded in the policy evaluator hot path. This couples policy logic to fallback orchestration and makes it hard to reason about backoff and retry strategies.
- Several upstream deps (protobufs and an in-house util package) are on older versions which prevent use of non-blocking data structures and newer atomic helpers.

Proposal:
1) Extract a lightweight "Fallback Transition Engine" with a clear interface (StartTransition, Observe, Cancel) implemented behind a pluggable adapter. The engine will run transitions off the hot path in a bounded worker pool and expose transition telemetry.
2) Replace the global regional mapper lock with fine-grained per-shard mutexes + optimistic read pass. For the high-frequency read path use an epoch-based snapshot combined with atomic CAS for writes.
3) Introduce a ring-buffer backed non-blocking fallback-queue (or use java.util.concurrent/folly ring buffer on C++ side) to decouple request enqueueing from processing.
4) Upgrade protobufs and internal util to enable VarHandle-like atomics and upgrade tracing lib to v2.1 for structured fallback traces.
5) Add focused unit and integration tests plus a localized load test harness (k6 script + synthetic routing traffic) to measure gains.

Acceptance criteria:
- 95th tail routing decision latency reduced by at least 20% in our staging benchmark for target workload A (chat generation, short prompts).
- CPU saturation under peak synthetic load reduced by 15% on the regional-mapper service.
- No regression in correctness: canary rollout shows identical routing decisions for pinned test traffic when fallback is disabled, and graceful fallback when enabled.
- New transition engine exposes metrics: fallback_started, fallback_succeeded, fallback_failed, fallback_duration_ms.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (small): implement adapters and wire to staging with feature flag routing.modular_fallback=true. Smoke tests + unit tests.
- Phase 2 (canary): enable for 5% of traffic in staging->internal canary, measure telemetry for 72 hours.
- Phase 3 (gradual): 25% -> 50% -> 100% in production over 7 days if telemetry tolerances met. Automated rollback on metric threshold breach.

Risks and mitigations:
- Behavioral drift: keep a deterministic simulation harness and a parity test comparing decisions vs legacy path for a sampled subset.
- Paging increases: worker pool bounded to avoid memory explosion; backpressure applied via token bucket.
- Dependency upgrade breakage: isolate upgrades behind compatibility interfaces and run full regression suite in CI.

- Proto changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/12480
- Benchmark harness (k6 scripts + infra): https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/tree/main/routing
